events.excerpt: Summary This proposal introduces post-quantum signature aggregation with leanVM in shadow mode . BLS remains the only authority for aggregates: consensus validity depends on BLS alone, exactly as today. leanVM aggregates and proofs are produced and verified alongside BLS, but their results have no effect on consensus. They are only measured, compared, and reported. When PQ/AI day arrives, an emergency hard fork simply retires BLS and enables leanVM in full. By “PQ/AI day” we mean the point at which quantum computers, or AI-assisted cryptanalysis, make BLS unsafe to rely on. Motivation Ethereum has to be ready for post-quantum signatures well before BLS is actually broken. Waiting until the last moment would mean deploying new, complex code to mainnet in a hurry. Giving leanVM authority early has its own risk: leanVM is new code that hasn’t been tested in production. However carefully it is built and audited, we can’t rule out a soundness bug that accepts an invalid proof, or a liveness bug that rejects a valid one. The main benefit of shadow mode is that Ethereum isn’t put at risk from a leanVM bug before PQ/AI day arrives. Because leanVM has no authority, a leanVM bug can’t break Ethereum’s security or halt the chain. At the same time, leanVM runs on mainnet under real load, so
events.headline: EIP Draft: Run leanVM aggregation in shadow mode alongside BLS until PQ/AI day

Overview Previously, we have presented our analyses of the equilibrium and dynamic simulation of EIP-7999’s multidimensional fee market, comparison with the post-Glamsterdam one-dimensional fee market . The strongest is floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 given the current resource demand , which we call the normalized benchmark in the paper: the transaction floor price is adjusted to each propagation allocation, and EIP-8372 scales CPSB and the state gas limit by a common factor, so that regular gas and state gas reach their targets at the same base fee in equilibrium. It keeps the EIP-1559 target-to-limit ratio of 1/2 and the EIP-1559 update rule. events.excerpt: Video game controllers have come a long way from the days when a vibration motor was enough to make the action in the game feel real. Modern controllers can simulate everything from the recoil of a gun to the resistance of pulling a bowstring — but there's still something missing. They can't reproduce the finer details of touching and handling objects in a virtual world. Researchers from Hunan University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences are looking to change that with ElectroPad , a modified PlayStation 5 controller that makes virtual objects feel more realistic. ElectroPad uses a technique called electrotactile stimulation. By sending carefully controlled electrical pulses through electrodes in contact with the skin, it can create localized sensations that mimic textures, edges, and shapes. The idea is to let players feel the surface of a virtual object as their character interacts with it, rather than simply experiencing a generic vibration. To make this possible, the researchers developed a pair of custom covers that fit over the handles of Sony's DualSense controller. Each cover is just 2 millimeters thick but contains 190 individually addressable electrodes, giving the complete controller an impressive 380 stimulation points. The electrodes are arranged to match the areas
events.headline: ElectroPad Makes Virtual Worlds Feel More Real

Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further. events.excerpt: The recently-unveiled Azume One , designed to turn almost any watch into a health-tracking smartwatch, hasn't even closed its crowdfunding campaign before receiving stiff competition in the form of the HIYD — a rival watch accessory that has it beat on size. "HIYD is a small waterproof and magnet-free sensor that attaches under your watch," Salah Batroukh, Hiyd chief executive officer, says of his company's inaugural product. "It tracks your sleep, recovery, heart, nutrition and more. No notifications or distractions. Earlier this year, we put our field prototype (which we called our Gen 1) into the hands of real customers and testers. Their feedback shaped everything we did next—and today, we’re excited to kick-start the HIYD Gen 2!" The idea behind the HIYD — first or second generation — is simple: it's a compact standalone sensor that attaches to the rear of most standard watches via a micro-suction backing, turning it into at least half of a smartwatch. "Half," because it's not designed to provide notifications nor add a display to the device; instead, it simply monitors the user's heart rate and blood oxygen concentration using a photoplethysmogram sensor, skin temperature, and movement via an accelerometer, transmitting the readings to a companion app running on the user's
events.headline: The Tiny HIYD Hides Behind Almost Any Watch to Deliver Real-Time Health, Fitness Tracking

events.excerpt: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationship with another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. events.excerpt: Hello Zcash Community! I have submitted a second Q4 retroactive grant application, for two pieces of Zebra security work. The first is my responsible disclosure of GHSA-4f6v-mj46-gxg3 , a Low severity vulnerability that let any peer delay the newest block on a Zebra node again and again without ever being banned. The Zcash Foundation published the advisory crediting me as the sole reporter, and the Zebra 6.4.0 release notes thank me by name for reporting it. The second is my fix to Zebra’s IPv6 peer limit, which let one cheap server fill all of a node’s connection slots. The Zcash Foundation then built on my fix to patch the Medium severity GHSA-jhpp-8h75-7pv5 , where a banned peer could come straight back from another address on the same server. The Zebra 6.4.0 release notes credit my issue for both the IPv6 limit and the ban fix. events.excerpt: Nvidia, which was the largest company in the world in terms of market cap until just days ago, is facing its biggest leadership crisis in years after reports of a second affair involving CEO Jensen Huang rattled the firm from the inside out. The latest development on the matter came out just minutes ago as fresh reports claimed that Huang has resigned in the wake of claims that he had multiple extramarital relationships, including with a woman who reports to him. The statement sent to media outlets says that Colette Kress, Nvidia’s current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. According to other reports, the company’s board met yesterday evening to address Huang’s future at the company, and the White House was aware of the meeting. Huang co-founded the Silicon Valley chipmaker in the early 1990s. He has been with the company ever since, and he presided over the firm during its spectacular rise amid the AI boom of the past several years. Nvidia’s stock has been under severe pressure lately, dropping from its all-time high of $239 in early October to $173 at yesterday’s close.
